bet.text: Play as many parts of the game as possible with a full-size robot, and hang off the side of the charge station on buddy forks for the triple balance.

demand.text: Score high, mid and low with both cones and cubes, and take cubes from the floor so low cube cycles are extremely efficient.
Its kickoff requirements sheet also lists cones from the double station, accurate auto movement, docking and engaging in auto and teleop, a side or late climb, and attaching to a partner to climb.

auto.text: Main routines are mobility and engage, two pieces, and three pieces, on the cable-guard side or the other. Waypoints are set relative to the start, so routines mirror and recalibrate quickly. PhotonVision corrects error, which the team says makes three pieces over the cable guard consistent.
Championship play averaged about 3 pieces in auto and 8.25 in teleop.

cycle.text: Cubes: floor intake, then straight to a low node, or the claw reaches in for mid and high. Cones: claw at the double station. An infrared sensor closes the claw. The operator picks a target on a numpad, the driver holds a button, and the robot routes there; gyro angle picks the arm side.

endgame.text: Two partners balance first. The robot comes to the side of the charge station, puts its forks under a partner and winches itself up, held only by that partner and the station. The team says the winch climbs in under 1 second and the triple balance takes under 10.

fallback.text: Pneumatic fork deployment, retraction and locking let the team abort a climb, and a pneumatic ratchet allows more than one try. The intake's shield lets it hold a cube and score low without the arm or claw.

gave_up.text: Full size (29 x 29 in) makes a triple balance and tight spaces harder; the team took that for stability at full arm extension and for playing through defense.
The forks came off before the first event, for weight and lack of programming time; the binder later counts several successful climbs.
A larger intake roller was faster in the open but worse at letting the claw move cubes sideways.

changed.text: After SE Mass a shield kept cubes out of the robot and opened low scoring without the claw. At Hartford a sequential handoff replaced a simultaneous one.

Carbon fork tubes deflected, so dowels and aluminum jackets were added. Cut cubes led to a pulley cover, then a planned belt guard. A claw and wrist over 2 lb lighter were made for fork weight; the binder lists them as backups.

outcome.text: 42-25-3 in official play; ranked 20 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 70.01, Hopper).

The team found the remaining backlash had minimal impact, because the arm always moves again before scoring

decisions.because: it plays through defense and is stable with the arm fully extended
decisions.cost: triple balance and tight areas of the field are harder
decisions.instead_of: a 26 x 26 in frame the team had planned and started, which became a packaging problem

decisions.because: in the January slides, three robots cannot easily fit on the charge station, and a fast last-second climb does not depend on partners' sizes
decisions.cost: the binder limits it by weight: a 125 lb robot needs a partner of 85 lb or more

decisions.because: taking the cube with the intake first and then reaching in with the claw was far more consistent
decisions.instead_of: claw and intake grabbing the cube at the same time

decisions.because: a pneumatic clamp needed precise grip height and centering on cones
decisions.instead_of: a pneumatic clamp with swiveling pads

decisions.choice: Belts in place of some claw wheels
decisions.because: squish wheels worked very well but a lighter claw was wanted
decisions.cost: the early belts quickly shed their Plastidip coating, and a cone met base-first could not be turned upright

decisions.because: it let them build the elevator in under two weeks once build season started
decisions.cost: the kit's bearing shoulder bolts deformed over time, and two blocks were redone with 1/4-20 bolts

decisions.choice: CAN bus wired in a mix of parallel and series, soldered wherever possible
decisions.because: one disconnected swerve pod motor cannot take down the rest of the bus
decisions.cost: at SE Mass a failed swerve pod CAN connection broke everything; motor inversions at boot, all season, looked like CAN errors but were probably a RoboRIO 2.0 buffer issue

decisions.choice: Positions relative to the auto start
decisions.because: routines mirror for alliance and side, and calibrate fast on a new field

decisions.choice: Use a foam roller on the cube intake
decisions.because: mecanum and squish wheels gripped so well that cubes stuck in the corners and the claw could not move them, and plain polycarbonate gripped too little
decisions.instead_of: mecanum and squish wheels, or a polycarbonate roller

decisions.because: the bumpers could easily push the charge station down
decisions.instead_of: locking the intake to slam the charge station down before driving over it

decisions.choice: Run a system check before every match
decisions.because: reliability became a focus after Hartford; the team reports no major field failures at the district championship or the championship
